newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Overseas borrowings by S.Korean financial firms up.
newsitem.headline: Overseas borrowings by S.Korean financial firms up.

text.p: South Korean financial institutions borrowed $2.68 billion in the first quarter of 1997 by issuing overseas bonds with more than five years maturity, a finance and economy ministry statement said on Friday.
The figure was up from $1.1 billion in the same period of last year.
State-owned Korea Development Bank issued a total of $1.15 billion worth of bonds during the period, the Korea Export-Import Bank of Korea, $1.45 billion, and Hanil Bank, $80 million.
The statement said interest rates on short-term borrowings rose slightly as Japanese banks reduced liquidity supply.
But Korean financial institutions faced no problem as the central Bank of Korea had released liquidity from its foreign currency reserves, it said.
